message: Hi Marco, thanks for joining. I'll be interviewing you for the Frontend Engineer role at Brightline Travel. We have about 5 minutes. To start, tell me briefly about your background and what drew you to this role.

Sure. I've been a frontend engineer for four years on an e-commerce storefront, React and TypeScript the whole time, and the last year and a half on Next.js. Travel booking is the same kind of problem, a long form with a lot of state and a payment at the end, so it felt like a natural next step.
You mentioned Next.js. Tell me about something you shipped on the App Router specifically: what it was and what you did.

Last spring we moved the product detail page from the Pages Router to the App Router. I owned that. I split the page into a server component that fetched the product and the inventory, and client components for the gallery and the add-to-cart button. The thing that bit us was caching: the inventory was getting cached by the fetch layer, so a sold-out size still showed as available. I set that fetch to no-store and kept the product data cached. After the move the page's time to first byte dropped from about 900 milliseconds to around 300.
How did you know the inventory was stale before customers did?

We didn't at first, a customer support ticket caught it in the first week. After that I added a check to our end-to-end suite that sets a size to zero stock through the admin API and asserts the button is disabled on the page, so it can't regress silently.
Let's talk about that suite. What end-to-end testing have you done, and with which tools?

I set up Playwright on the storefront about two years ago, there was only Jest before that. We have around sixty Playwright specs now, the core ones are the checkout flow, search, and the account pages. They run on every pull request against a preview deployment, and the flaky ones run in a separate retry job so they don't block merges. I wrote maybe half of them and I review the rest. The one I'm proudest of is the checkout test that stubs the payment provider's iframe, because that was the test everyone said couldn't be automated.
What do you do when one of those specs fails and you don't know if it's the test or the app?

First I look at the trace, Playwright records a trace with screenshots and network calls, so usually I can see whether the page did something different or the test waited on the wrong thing. If it's the test, I fix the selector or the wait and move on. If it's the app, I file it with the trace attached. I try not to add retries as the fix, because that's how a suite goes quiet.
That's a good place to stop, we're close to time. Thank you, Marco, your feedback will follow shortly.
